chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'My slave, if he steals from me, I do not cut him, and my slave, if he steals from others, I cut him, and the slave of the Emirate, if he steals, I do not cut him, because he is Fay' (war booty).'

key_terms.فَيْ‏ءٌ: Fay (war booty or state treasury assets)
key_terms.يَقْطَعُ: To cut (referring to the hadd punishment of amputation)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in hadd punishment for a personal slave versus a state slave who commits theft?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) articulates a nuanced legal distinction where a personal slave is exempt from hadd theft if they steal from their master, as the master effectively absorbs the loss, whereas a state-owned slave (fay') is punished for stealing from others because the property belongs to the public treasury. This ruling highlights the jurisprudential concept of 'ghasb' (usurpation) versus 'malik' (ownership) in determining liability, reflecting the administrative realities of the early Islamic state. It underscores the principle that the nature of the victim's ownership dictates the application of the fixed penalty.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘If myasws slave steals from measws, Iasws would not cut him, and if myasws slave steals from others, Iasws would cut him, and a slave of the emirate, if he were to steal, Iasws would not cut him because he is ‘Fey’ (war booty)’.
